turns.content: Let P be the parents' present combined age, C the children's present combined age, and n the number of children. Translate the statement that P is six times C.
How much do the parents' combined age and the children's combined age each change per calendar year? Express the rates in terms of the two parents and n children.
Explain how those group-level rates will be used consistently for both the past and future conditions.
Write the equation for the situation two years ago using the group-level rates.
Write the equation for the situation six years from now using the group-level rates.
Substitute the present-age relation established in the first turn into the past and future equations, and simplify both to relations between C and n.
Solve the resulting pair of relations for the number of children.
